pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind feature
/sig api-machinery
/wg apply
/priority important-soon
/cc @apelisse @lavalamp @kwiesmueller 

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Prevents the list of managers from growing too large.

also,
Fixes #82042

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
NONE
```

issue_context.title: Serialization of fieldsets in managedFields should always be the same
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:
The serialization of managedFields field sets can change, resulting in an otherwise no-op update causing a write to etcd. The issue arises when a fieldset like this
```
"k:{\"name\":\"test-container-a\"}": {
    ".": {},		
    "f:image": {},
    "f:name": {}
}
```
is decoded and re-encoded as part of a modifying request, which causes it to become
```
"k:{\"name\":\"test-container-a\"}": {
    "f:image": {},
    "f:name": {}
    ".": {},		
},
```

This isn't too serious, as it only seems to happen on the first update after a new list item is added, but we should try to understand this better and fix it.

**What you expected to happen**:
The fieldset serialization should be unaffected by round tripping through the internal structured-merge-diff type.

/sig api-machinery
/wg apply
/priority help-wanted
/cc @lavalamp @apelisse
comments: How did the first serialization happen? I think smd should always emit the "." last?

@@ -93,6 +94,8 @@ func (f *capManagersManager) capUpdateManagers(managed Managed) (newManaged Mana

        // Merge the oldest updaters with versioned bucket managers until the number of updaters is under the cap
        versionToFirstManager := map[string]string{}
+       originalLength := len(updaters)
+       startTime := time.Now()
        for i, length := 0, len(updaters); i < len(updaters) && length > f.maxUpdateManagers; i++ {
                manager := updaters[i]
                vs := managed.Fields()[manager]
@@ -130,6 +133,7 @@ func (f *capManagersManager) capUpdateManagers(managed Managed) (newManaged Mana
                        versionToFirstManager[version] = manager
                }
        }
+       klog.Infof("reduced the number of updaters from %v to %v in %v", originalLength, f.maxUpdateManagers, time.Now().Sub(startTime))

        return managed, nil
 }

This is only used in the `fieldmanager` package, can it be put into `internal`?

Putting this in internal means we couldn't construct a fieldmanager from outside of this package. Also I'm not sure if, being in internal, we would be allowed to implement the interface Manager, since it's functions take some interfaces defined in this package as arguments. This Manager is mostly just a wrapper for internal.BuildManagerIdentifier anyway, so most of the logic is internal
